subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should same-session hook-agent deliveries be rejected with 409, skipped, queued, or left parallel by default, and should any non-parallel behavior be opt-in per hook or mapping?
rationale: The requested 409 response changes the public webhook response contract and retry semantics, while the alternatives create different queueing and compatibility behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
options.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior and add a documented hook or mapping policy for reject, skip, or queue semantics keyed by the resolved sessionKey.

options.title: Make 409 The Default
options.body: Reject active same-session hook deliveries by default and accept that some existing senders may need migration to avoid retry storms.

options.title: Leave Locking To Callers
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's hook endpoint parallel and document idempotency keys plus caller-managed locks as the supported overlap control.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
recommendation.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior and add a documented hook or mapping policy for reject, skip, or queue semantics keyed by the resolved sessionKey.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior issue review framed this exact behavior as a maintainer product/security policy choice, making Peter the best available decision owner from the reviewed evidence.
